title: Russia and Ukraine Agree to Large Prisoner Exchange as Abu Dhabi Talks End Without Breakthrough
dek: U.S.-mediated talks produced a prisoner-swap agreement, but no progress on a ceasefire or territory. Numbers are due Thursday.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Skyline of Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates

keyPoints: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, the Associated Press reported.
Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky described the swap as agreed "in principle"; U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said the final number would be set Thursday.
Russia’s state news agency TASS reported the exchange should happen in two to three weeks.
Kushner called the talks "very tough" but "productive," and said territory would be the hardest issue to settle.
body:
Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war on Wednesday, both sides said, as two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a breakthrough toward ending the war, [the Associated Press reported](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/11/g-s1-152954/russia-ukraine-war-talks).

## What was agreed

Russia’s chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, said at the talks that both sides had agreed on a large-scale prisoner swap and that understanding had been reached on some issues, [Al Jazeera reported](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/11/russia-ukraine-talks-in-abu-dhabi-end-with-prisoner-exchange-agreement). Medinsky noted the agreement was "in principle." U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said the number of prisoners would be finalized on Thursday.

The Russian state news agency TASS reported the exchange should take place in two to three weeks. Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia said there was "good momentum" toward a solution before the end of the year.

## What was not

The talks were the first meeting between the delegations in nine months, according to the Associated Press, and the sides were far apart. Territory, the fate of Russian-occupied Ukrainian land and postwar security guarantees remain unresolved. Kushner said territorial questions would be the hardest to settle, but that progress had been made on a post-war security framework.

## Next steps

Kushner and U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff said they would travel to Moscow on Thursday to brief President Vladimir Putin, then fly to Dublin to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, [Al Jazeera reported](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/11/russia-ukraine-talks-in-abu-dhabi-end-with-prisoner-exchange-agreement). Medinsky said more talks would be held soon and that Moscow was not opposed to European Union participation, while questioning what Russia and the EU would discuss.

Analysts cited by Al Jazeera said exchanges of this kind have happened regularly, and that this one would need to top the 1,000-for-1,000 swap of May 2025 to be the largest. That comparison is an analyst view, not an official figure.

The final prisoner count has not been announced.
